speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing neck and arm pain, paresthesias, and muscle weakness. To help me determine the cause, can you tell me if your symptoms started suddenly or developed gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The gradual onset of burning pain and paresthesias worsening with muscle weakness in both hands is concerning. Given your history of diabetes, hypertension, and the specific location of symptoms, have you noticed any numbness or tingling radiating specifically down into your fingers?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) with cervical myelopathy. The combination of progressive upper and lower motor neuron signs (fasciculations, weakness, absent reflexes) alongside burning pain and paresthesias is highly suggestive of ALS, though the burning pain and sensory symptoms could indicate a concurrent cervical cord compression (myelopathy). I will proceed with imaging to rule out compressive lesions. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Cervical_Spine. REQUEST TEST: EMG/NCS.
